title: stalled-promotion-due-to-index-sync-failure-and-eviction-throttle-mitigation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
summary: During a multi-stage model promotion we observed a stalled promotion state where traffic remained pinned to the old model for a subset of regions. The immediate cause was a metadata index sync failure between the rollout orchestrator and the edge route translator, which triggered eviction-throttle behavior in the serving pool and prevented the promotion from completing. This ticket collates the post-incident investigation, short-term mitigations already applied, and proposed longer-term actions to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: At 2026-03-05T14:12 UTC a scheduled canary promotion was initiated for model v2026-03-b. Canary traffic passed health checks in primary region, but ~12% of production requests (cross-region) continued to be routed to the previous version. Attempts to complete the promotion reported pin conflicts. The orchestrator and route translator had diverging deployment index versions: the translator had not received the latest route-index update due to a partial failure in the index-broadcast worker. Simultaneously, eviction-throttle in the serving pool engaged when pods attempted to reconcile pinned state, causing capacity churn and preventing forced unpin operations.
timeline: 2026-03-05T14:12 UTC - Promotion start: v2026-03-b canary at 5%
2026-03-05T14:18 UTC - Health checks green in region-us-west; rollout commanded to proceed
2026-03-05T14:21 UTC - Operator observed inconsistent routing metrics: traffic not fully shifting in eu-west
2026-03-05T14:24 UTC - Automated promotion state machine reported pin conflict when applying new route index
2026-03-05T14:26 UTC - On-call triggered manual verification: orchestrator index version 87, translator index version 82
2026-03-05T14:30 UTC - Index-broadcast worker logs show intermittent RPC timeouts to translator fleet (5s timeouts) during window
2026-03-05T14:35 UTC - Serving pool eviction-throttle threshold hit after repeated reconcile attempts, causing pod restarts in eu-west
2026-03-05T14:50 UTC - Emergency fallback: degrade to pinned-old across eu-west to stabilize latency (manual rollback of partial promotion)
2026-03-05T15:10 UTC - Incident declared; mitigation: restart index-broadcast worker and apply forced reconciler to translator nodes
2026-03-05T15:40 UTC - Translator index reconciled to orchestrator; routing stabilized; full promotion resumed after additional verification
2026-03-05T16:05 UTC - Promotion completed; monitoring period initiated for 2h
root_cause: The index-broadcast worker that pushes deployment index updates to the route translator experienced transient RPC failures that were not retried aggressively. This left the translator with a stale index version. When the orchestrator attempted to complete the promotion, conflicting pin state and repeated reconcile attempts triggered eviction-throttle protections in the serving pool, which in turn prevented the reconciler from making progress and blocked promotion completion. There was also insufficient pre-promotion verification for index consistency across critical translator replicas.
contributing_factors: index-broadcast worker: single-threaded loop with limited retries and no backoff escalation
route translator: no target-version liveness check before accepting promotion commands
serving pool eviction-throttle: threshold designed to protect stability but lacked explicit exception path for reconciler-driven operations
monitoring gap: no synthetic check that validated index parity across regions prior to promotion
operational playbook: missing an explicit forced-reconcile procedure for translator index drift
mitigations_implemented: restarted index-broadcast worker with patched RPC client to increase retry count and exponential backoff (hotfix deployed 2026-03-05T15:12 UTC)
deployed temporary reconciler job with elevated rate limits to re-push index to translator replicas in eu-west (2026-03-05T15:18 UTC)
tuned eviction-throttle window to allow reconciler-driven unpin operations to proceed during rollouts (temporary config change applied)
added alert: index-version-drift (>1) between orchestrator and translator replicas (alert rule created)
manual runbook: documented emergency unpin steps and surfaced to SRE rotation
action_items: ENG-99577-A: Implement a two-phase promotion preflight that verifies index parity across >95% translator replicas before advancing to global promotion - owner: Tomás Ortega - due: 2026-03-20

ENG-99577-B: Rework index-broadcast worker to be multi-threaded with durable queueing (persisted message queue) and idempotent apply semantics; include exponential backoff and circuit-breaker - owner: Priya Menon - due: 2026-04-03
ENG-99577-C: Introduce a reconciler exemption in eviction-throttle that recognizes reconciler JWT and allows controlled unpin operations - owner: SRE Team (lead: Marcus Lee) - due: 2026-03-27

ENG-99577-D: Extend canary preflight to run a parity synthetic that performs read-after-write verification on routing index and KV pin state in all target regions - owner: QA (lead: Lena Fischer) - due: 2026-03-18

ENG-99577-E: Add a dashboard panel that surfaces per-region index-version histogram and time-since-last-sync; wire to a paging alert when distribution skew exceeds threshold - owner: Observability (lead: Omar Reyes) - due: 2026-03-22

ENG-99577-F: Update rollout runbook with explicit forced-reconcile recipe and post-reconcile verification steps; include GitHub PR link to runbook draft - owner: Tomás Ortega - due: 2026-03-12 (draft done)

ENG-99577-G: Post-incident test: run 10 simulated promotions across 3 regions under induced packet loss to validate new broadcast/reconcile behavior - owner: Reliability (lead: Jia Chen) - due: 2026-04-10
monitoring_checks: index-parity-synthetic: write small unique change then confirm index version increments on all translator replicas within 10s
eviction-throttle-exception-metric: track reconciler-tagged unpin ops allowed per window
promotion-latency-SLO: time between 'promote start' and 'global completion' should be < 5 minutes for non-fallback promotions
routing-staleness-alert: page when >3% of requests in a region see older model version for >2 minutes after promotion step
